title: Local integer and adic separation criterion for linearity
statement: Let J be a Grothendieck topology on C, l a natural number, S and R ring sheaves, c:S≅R a ring-sheaf isomorphism, N an S-module sheaf and P an R-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume that for every section r of S and every n, the integer approximation sieve [lem-sfb-completed-coefficient-local-integers] for l^(n+1) covers, and that any section of P whose image sieves under every l^(n+1) cover is zero. Then every additive sheaf map g:N_ab→P_ab satisfies g(r x)=c(r)g(x) on every object. The approximation and separation hypotheses are explicit assumptions, not additional conclusions.

source.place: sectionwise form of the integer-modulo-powers action-defect criterion; proof step 3 of lem-sfb-diagonal-completed-free-generator

proof.text: For each n restrict to the covering integer-approximation sieve. Write the restricted scalar r=a+l^(n+1)b. Naturality restricts g(r x)-c(r)g(x) to g((a+l^(n+1)b)y)-c(a+l^(n+1)b)g(y).

Distribute both actions and use additivity of g, preservation of integer multiples by g, preservation of integers by c, and compatibility of natural multiples with module actions. The integer terms cancel and the defect becomes l^(n+1) times g(by)-c(b)g(y). This is an explicit preimage witness, so the power-image sieve contains the covering approximation sieve.
Apply the assumed adic separation criterion to the action defect. Its every power-image sieve covers, so it vanishes. Subtraction by zero gives the asserted equality.

proof_origin.place: direct sectionwise proof of the local approximation/separated-target criterion

mathlib_searches.query: A section of the sheaf of p-adic integer coefficients is locally an integer plus p to the n times another section, using the finite cyclic quotient sheaf
mathlib_searches.results: PadicInt.appr_spec, PadicInt.lift_sub_val_mem_span, PadicInt.toZMod_spec and related pointwise ring approximation lemmas; no theorem for the reconstructed ring sheaf. The local source analogue PadicInt.exists_isOpen_eq_intCast_add_pow_mul treats concrete continuous functions, whereas the existing quotient comparison directly applies to the reconstructed coefficients.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Use the existing sheaf quotient calculation and its normalized finite projection, rather than introducing a separate comparison with a concrete continuous-function sheaf.

mathlib_searches.results: map_zsmul and AddMonoidHom.map_zsmul preserve integer multiples. These give the algebraic part, not local integer approximation or free-sheaf separation.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Use integer-multiple preservation in the combination argument.

mathlib_searches.results: No relevant Mathlib free-sheaf separation theorem. Source PadicIntSheafLinear provides the action-defect criterion; PadicIntLatticeLisse applies it only to finite free targets. Local searches of Sheaf found no local-integer or free-adic-separation statement.
mathlib_searches.verdict: The needed coefficient and target assertions are not duplicates of existing statements.

lean.statement:
theorem linearity_of_localIntegers_adicSeparated
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (l : ℕ) {S R : Sheaf J RingCat.{w}} (c : S ≅ R)
    (N : SheafOfModules.{t} S) (P : SheafOfModules.{t} R)
    (g : (SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj N ⟶ (SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj P)
    (hlocal : ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Cᵒᵖ) (r : S.obj.obj V),
      integerApproximationSieve S (l ^ (n + 1)) r ∈ J V.unop)
    (hsep : ∀ (V : Cᵒᵖ) (z : P.val.obj V),
      (∀ n : ℕ, Presheaf.imageSieve
        ((l ^ (n + 1) • 𝟙 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf R).obj P)).hom) z ∈ J V.unop) →
        z = 0)
    (V : Cᵒᵖ) (r : S.obj.obj V) (x : N.val.obj V) :
    g.hom.app V (r • x) =
      @SMul.smul _ (P.val.obj V) inferInstance (c.hom.hom.app V r) (g.hom.app V x)
